verdict: Figma grew revenue 43% to $391M as customers bought more seats and AI credits, but heavy stock pay from its recent IPO kept GAAP results at an $81M loss — excluding stock pay, operations earned $47M.

segments.name: Subscriptions & AI credits
segments.note: Design-tool subscriptions (per-seat plans for Figma, Dev Mode, Make and Sites) plus usage credits for AI features. Figma reports one revenue stream.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Building the design platform and its AI features — the biggest cost by far, and heavy with stock pay.

opex.name: Sales & marketing
opex.note: Selling seats to design and product teams.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Running the company day to day — also heavy with post-IPO stock pay.

takeaways.title: Growth beat its own guidance
takeaways.text: Revenue of $391M grew 43% and topped Figma's guidance range; management raised the full-year outlook to about $1.50B as AI features turned into paid credits.

takeaways.title: Stock pay is the story
takeaways.text: Stock-based compensation was about $159M in the quarter — more than the entire gap between the $119M GAAP operating loss and the $47M non-GAAP operating profit.

takeaways.title: Big customers keep joining
takeaways.text: Customers paying over $10k a year rose by more than 3,650 in a year to 16,566 — and over 80% of them now consume AI credits every week.

oneTimers: Figma listed on the NYSE in July 2025. Newly public companies often show giant GAAP losses as years of employee stock awards vest at once: Q3 2025's loss was $1,097M for exactly that reason. This quarter's $81M loss is the same effect, fading.
otherDetail: Other income of $47M, net — mostly interest earned on the cash Figma raised in its 2025 IPO.
follow100Note: Rows add up with a small rounding difference. Costs ran to $120.78 per $100 of revenue — the extra is the loss, covered by cash the company already had.
